newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel market quiet, waits for crude to settle.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel market quiet, waits for crude to settle.

text.p: Jittery crude futures dampened activity on the NWE cracked fuel oil market.
"No one is selling at fixed prices, it could lose you your job," said one trader.
"I think everything needs to settle down before we see much trading," added another trader.

High sulphur barges traded in a range between $113-116 fob ARA, before settling around $115 a tonne. There was some talk of a shortage of refinery material and bunker demand was deemed to be "there, but not healthy," according to one barge dealer.

The high sulphur cracked cargo market was pegged at $114-116 cif NWE, marginally higher than Wednesday. But the rise has scarced off buying interest that emerged yesterday. The north looks a touch long, a situation that could be exacerbated by good supplies in the Med which may have to move northwards.

The low sulphur cracked market slipped a touch with offers heard as low as $136 cif Med. One NWE cargo that was thought destined for the U.S. was offered into the Med. In NWE paper levels were weaker with $126.25 done on January paper.
